headline: Revenue growth continues, profit jumps on lower share count
summary_short: CCC Intelligent Solutions grew Q2 2026 revenue 9.8% y/y to $285.9M, with net income up 60.4% y/y to $20.8M ($0.04 diluted EPS) as software-subscription growth and a smaller share count following recent buybacks lifted results.
summary_long: Revenue rose 9.8% y/y to $285.9M, about 7 points from existing-customer upgrades/expansion and 2 points from new customers. Gross margin slipped to 73.7% from 74.5% on higher IT and personnel costs even as gross profit grew 8.6%. R&D fell 11.6% on more capitalized development time, helping operating income rise 94.7% y/y. Net income more than doubled to $20.8M on that leverage plus lower interest-rate-swap valuations, despite $2.5M higher interest expense from a Q4-2025 term-loan add-on. Adjusted EBITDA was $115.5M (40% margin, down from 42%). No buybacks this quarter; $100M remains available under the $500M program. Cash was $115.9M; term loan $1,284.5M, revolver undrawn. No forward guidance was issued.

drivers.explanation: Growth was about 7 points from existing-customer upgrades and expanded solution adoption and about 2 points from new customers; software subscriptions were 96% of total revenue.
Dollar growth came from higher software subscription revenue and fixed-cost operating leverage, but margin slipped to 73.7% from 74.5% as IT, third-party fee and personnel costs outpaced revenue.
R&D expense fell 11.6% on more capitalized development time and lower stock-based compensation, while selling/marketing and G&A were roughly flat, letting profit growth outpace revenue.

Tracks the same cost discipline as operating income; y/y outperformance versus operating income reflects a swing in other income (interest-rate swap fair-value gains) sitting below the operating line.
Sequential dip versus Q1 2026 is not explained in the release; y/y growth reflects the same revenue growth and cost discipline cited for operating income.

Higher operating profit plus $2.6M of other income from lower interest-rate-swap valuations drove the gain, despite a $17.0M larger income tax provision and $2.5M higher interest expense from the Q4-2025 term-loan add-on.
Software Net Dollar Retention held at 107% y/y while Software Gross Dollar Retention softened to 98% from 99%, indicating stable expansion revenue alongside slightly higher customer churn.
